architecture.description: Slice of a universal binary (arm64, arm64e, x86_64, ...); arm64, then x86_64, then the first when omitted.

path.description: Absolute path of a Mach-O file or app bundle; the active target when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_nib_decode
tools.description: Decode compiled nib and storyboard files (NIB archives and keyed-archive nibs; .nib, .storyboardc and whole app bundles) into object graphs: objects with classes and values, outlet and action connections, and the view hierarchy. Bounded by max_documents, max_objects and max_connections.

path.description: Absolute path of a .nib file, .nib or .storyboardc folder, or app bundle; the active target when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_objc_classes_list
tools.description: Deduplicated Objective-C class and category names (with method counts), optionally filtered by a substring.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

pattern.description: Only names containing this (case-insensitive); everything when empty.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_objc_protocols_list
tools.description: Objective-C protocols with their methods, plus Swift protocols from symbols.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_plist_show
tools.description: Read a property list (XML or binary) as normalised JSON: a .plist file, an app bundle's Info.plist, or the Info.plist embedded in a Mach-O executable. Uses the active target unless path is given.

path.description: Absolute path of a file or app bundle; the active target when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_signature_show
tools.description: Decode a Mach-O code signature: code directories (identifier, team id, flags, hash type, slot counts, cdhash), page and special-slot hashes re-computed and compared, requirements as text, entitlements, and whether a CMS signature is present. The CMS signature itself is not verified.

architecture.description: Slice of a universal binary (arm64, arm64e, x86_64, ...); arm64, then x86_64, then the first when omitted.

path.description: Absolute path of a Mach-O file or app bundle; the active target when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_slices_list
tools.description: List the architecture slices of a thin or universal Mach-O (CPU type and subtype, offset, size, alignment, file type).

path.description: Absolute path of a file or app bundle; the active target when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_swift_symbols_demangle
tools.description: Turn mangled Swift symbol names into readable declarations, in order, each marked demangled, unchanged (not a Swift name) or invalid. Built-in demangler; no target needed.

symbols.description: Mangled names, one per entry (1–10000; single line, no NUL).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_swift_types_list
tools.description: Swift symbols grouped into classes, structs, enums, protocols, extensions and other, by type path and role (accessor, descriptor, method...).

category.description: classes, structs, enums, protocols, extensions or other.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

pattern.description: Only type paths containing this (case-insensitive).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__apple_ui_action_trace
tools.description: UI action or selector (e.g. `saveDocument:`) → handlers (Objective-C methods, matching names, code using the string) → the static calls they make, bounded by max_depth/max_nodes/max_edges. Best effort; limits are listed.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__assets_image_generate
tools.description: Make a picture with fal.ai (Nano Banana Pro) and save it as a PNG inside app/: a texture, a sky or background, an icon, a title screen or concept art. shape: square (1024x1024, default), wide (1024x576) or tall (576x1024). Costs about $0.15, counted against the project's asset budget. Describe original designs in the original's style; never ask for recognisable characters, logos or brand artwork. Returns where it was saved, the cost and the budget left.

prompt.description: What to draw, in detail (subject, style, colours, lighting).

save_as.description: Where to save it, relative to app/, ending in .png (e.g. Assets/Textures/crate.png).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__assets_key_remove
tools.description: Remove an asset provider's stored key (`provider`, default fal).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__assets_key_set
tools.description: Store an asset provider's key (`provider`, default fal) for generated pictures and 3D models in the system keychain (or the private key file). It's never shown again or written to logs.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__assets_key_status
tools.description: Whether each asset provider (fal.ai today) has a key for generated pictures and 3D models, stored or in its environment variable. `stored` answers for `provider` (default fal). Keys themselves are never shown.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__assets_model_generate
tools.description: Make a game-ready, low-poly 3D model (GLB) with fal.ai (Tripo P1) and save it inside app/. Give a prompt (a picture is made first, then turned into the model) or an image (a web address, or a picture inside the project such as reference/picture-1.png). faces caps the face count (48 to 20000, default 3000): about 500-1500 for small props and pickups, 2000-5000 for weapons, furniture and vehicles, 6000-15000 for main characters; fewer faces run faster, so use the fewest that still look right. textured (default true) gives colours and surfaces. A textured model costs $0.50 plus $0.15 for the picture, counted against the project's asset budget; it takes a minute or two. Describe one original object per model; never ask for recognisable characters, logos or brand artwork. Returns where it was saved, the cost and the budget left.

faces.description: Most faces the model may have, 48 to 20000 (default 3000). Fewer faces run faster.

image.description: A picture to turn into the model: a web address, or a picture inside the project.

prompt.description: What to make: one object, described in detail. Used when no image is given.

save_as.description: Where to save it, relative to app/, ending in .glb (e.g. Assets/Models/crate.glb).

textured.description: Colours and surfaces (default true); false makes a plain grey model for $0.40 instead of $0.50.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__build_checklist
tools.description: Show the person your plan as a short checklist and keep it current: todos with content (a plain step), activeForm ("Drawing the map") and status (pending, in_progress or completed). Call it again whenever a step changes; the app pins it above the prompt box.

activeForm.description: What it says while doing it ("Drawing the map").

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__build_command_run
tools.description: Run a command in app/ (npm install, npm run build, cargo build, the game engine's build...) and return its exit code and the end of its output. Common build commands go ahead; dev servers and watchers are refused (they never exit); anything else asks the person. Default limit 10 minutes, at most 2 hours.

command.description: The command, run in app/ (`&&` joins steps).

timeout_secs.description: Time limit in seconds (default 600, at most 7200).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__build_file_edit
tools.description: Replace exact text in a file: old_text must appear exactly once (or set replace_all). Inside app/ this goes ahead; anywhere else asks the person.

path.description: A file relative to the project.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of exactly one.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__build_file_read
tools.description: Read a text file in the project (app/, capture/, reference/...), paged by lines with offset/limit for big files.

limit.description: How many lines (default: up to 256 KB).

path.description: A file relative to the project, e.g. `app/src/main.rs` or `capture/README.md`.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__build_file_write
tools.description: Create or replace a text file. Inside app/ this goes ahead; anywhere else asks the person.

path.description: A file relative to the project, e.g. `app/src/main.rs`.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__build_files_list
tools.description: List files and folders in the app: app/ usually, or the project folder when the app is edited in place. A few levels deep; paths are relative to the project folder; build output and dependencies (node_modules, target, vendor, dist...) are skipped.

depth.description: How many levels down (default 4, at most 8).

path.description:
A folder relative to the project (default: the app folder; for a project edited in
place, the project folder itself).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_archive_extract
tools.description: Extract every regular file of a ZIP/APK/IPA/JAR or ASAR (plus its .asar.unpacked files) into a fresh private temporary folder chosen by Craft Anything, and return its path. Bounded size and count; entries that would escape the folder are refused.

if_tampered.description: What to do when an ASAR integrity hash or ZIP CRC does not match.

path.description: Absolute path of the ZIP/APK/IPA/JAR or ASAR. Defaults to the active target.

oneOf.description: Stop with an error when a recorded hash or checksum does not match the content.
Record mismatches as contradictions and keep going.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_archive_show
tools.description: Content-addressed inventory of a ZIP/APK/IPA/JAR, Electron ASAR, app bundle or folder: every file with size, kind, role and sha256; nested archives opened to a bounded depth; ASAR integrity hashes and ZIP CRCs checked. Paged (offset/limit).

if_tampered.description: What to do when an ASAR integrity hash or ZIP CRC does not match.

max_depth.description: How deep nested archives are opened (0–6).

max_total_bytes.description: Most bytes read and hashed in total.

path.description: Absolute path of the archive, app bundle or folder. Defaults to the active target.

oneOf.description: Stop with an error when a recorded hash or checksum does not match the content.
Record mismatches as contradictions and keep going.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_archives_compare
tools.description: Compare two archives, app bundles or folders file by file: added, removed, changed (by sha256) and moved files. Inputs are absolute paths or core_archive_show evidence.

left.description: The older artifact: an absolute path, or core_archive_show evidence (inline or {"kind":"saved","evidence_id":...}).

right.description: The newer artifact, in the same forms.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_brief_write
tools.description: Set the investigation brief: the question, purpose, targets, constraints and what 'done' means. Write it before the first analysis call on a new question.

constraints.description: Constraints (clean room, no running the target, time budget...).

done_when.description: What a finished answer looks like.

purpose.description: Why the user is asking (interoperability, security review, learning...).

question.description: The question being answered, in one or two sentences.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_evidence_browse
tools.description: View part of a stored (or inline) evidence record: the summary, one part, one row of a list, a page of a list's rows (optionally only the rows matching given field values, cut to chosen fields, with the field names listed), or a part of a function dossier (pseudocode, assembly, basic_blocks, callers, callees, flow_*...), with coverage and next_offset. Nothing is analysed again.

show.description: What part of it to show.

oneOf.description: Evidence already recorded in this session or project.
A full evidence record passed inline.
The record without its result.
One named part of the result (e.g. mitigations, linkage).
One row of a list: by index, or the first whose name/address equals `pick`.
A page of a list (sections, symbols, functions...).

field_names.description: Also list the field names of the matching rows, to see what to match or pick.

fields.description: Return only these fields of each row (`a.b` reaches inside); a row without one leaves it out.

matching.description:
Keep only the rows whose fields equal these values, e.g. `{"kind": "require", "path":
["main.js", "preload.js"]}`: every field must match, a list means any of its values,
`a.b` reaches inside a row and null matches a field the row doesn't have.

offset.description: Counts matching rows when `matching` is given.

oneOf.description:
A part of a native function dossier (pseudocode, assembly, basic_blocks, callers, callees,
incoming_references, outgoing_references, unresolved_calls, referenced_strings,
referenced_names, native_api, flow_summary, flow_nodes,
flow_edges, flow_effects, flow_parameters, flow_parameter_uses,
comments, function). Text facets page by UTF-16 units.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_evidence_export
tools.description: Write every evidence record and unknown to a JSON bundle file.

path.description: Absolute path of the bundle file to write.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_evidence_exports_compare
tools.description: Compare two exported evidence bundles (core_evidence_export files) and report which records were added, removed or changed, matched by operation and subject. Every record is checked against its own id, so one edited after export is reported, never counted as unchanged.

keep_pairs.description: Include the matched record-id pairs in the result.

newer_bundle.description: Absolute path to the second evidence bundle.

older_bundle.description: Absolute path to the first evidence bundle.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_evidence_import
tools.description: Load a bundle written by core_evidence_export. Tampered records are rejected.

path.description: Absolute path of a bundle file.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_evidence_show
tools.description: All evidence recorded in this session (detail=summary for a compact list; filter by operation or evidence_id).

operation.description: Only records produced by this operation.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_feature_find
tools.description: Literal text → matching strings, functions and imports → the code that uses them → the functions involved.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

query.description: Text to look for (e.g. a label or message you see in the app).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_finding_edit
tools.description: Correct a recorded finding without changing its id. Requires a statement and existing evidence ids; pass based_on_revision to refuse a stale investigation update.

based_on_revision.description: The investigation revision read before editing; a stale revision is refused.

confidence.description: Omit to keep the finding's current confidence.

evidence_ids.description: Evidence ids that establish the corrected answer (at least one).

finding_id.description: An existing finding id from core_investigation_show.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_finding_record
tools.description: Record a settled answer. Requires at least one evidence id; every id is checked against the ledger. Findings are the source for reports.

confidence.description: observed (read directly), derived (computed from observations) or inferred (best guess).

evidence_ids.description: Evidence ids that establish it (at least one).

statement.description: The settled answer, in one or two sentences.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_handoff_write
tools.description: Rewrite the handoff note: where we are, what's next, traps to avoid. Write it at the end of every turn so the next turn (or agent) resumes without re-deriving.

text.description: Where we are, what's next, and traps to avoid. Replaces the previous handoff.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_hypothesis_record
tools.description: Record a claim being tested, ideally with the prediction that would confirm or refute it, plus any supporting/contradicting evidence ids.

prediction.description: What we expect to observe if the claim is true.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_hypothesis_update
tools.description: Change a hypothesis's status (testing/supported/refuted/abandoned) and attach supporting or contradicting evidence ids and notes.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_investigation_show
tools.description: The working memory of this investigation: brief, plan with step status, hypotheses, findings (with evidence ids) and the latest handoff. Read it first when starting or resuming.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_journal_read
tools.description: Page through the project's append-only journal (tool calls, model turns, consents, errors), filtered by day, kind or tool. Needs an open project.

day.description: Day to read (`YYYY-MM-DD`); the latest day when omitted.

kind.description: Only entries of this kind (`tool_call`, `model_turn`, `consent`, `user_message`, `error`...).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_overview_show
tools.description: One-page summary of a program: format, architecture, entry, segments, counts of functions/strings/imports/exports, libraries, hardening, toolchain hints. detail=summary keeps the full record and returns counts plus a reference to page with core_evidence_browse.

detail.description:
complete (default) returns the full record; summary returns counts plus a reference to page
with core_evidence_browse.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

Detail.description:
The uniform summary-first detail control (see the module docs). `complete` is the default and
returns the full evidence record; `summary` returns a compact, pageable view.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_packed_files_list
tools.description: List the files carried inside one program or game file, recognised from its bytes (the reader used is in the result; `format` picks one when a file could be read several ways). Results give each member's path, size, how it's stored and what the file says it is, plus the facts of that kind of file, paged with offset/limit. `contains` keeps paths holding that text. For ordinary archives and app bundles use core_archive_show. Nothing is executed.

contains.description: Keep only members whose path contains this text.

format.description: Read the file as this kind (a reader id) instead of recognising it.

path.description: Absolute path of the file; the active target when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_packed_files_unpack
tools.description: Write files carried inside one program or game file into a new folder (output_directory must not exist yet; it is created). `paths` picks exact members, `contains` those holding some text; with neither, all of them. Never overwrites; a member whose path would leave the folder is skipped and named. Bounded by max_output_bytes and max_output_files. Writes manifest.json with every member's SHA-256 (under another name, given in the result, if a packed file took that one). Nothing is executed.

contains.description: Take out members whose path contains this text.

format.description: Read the file as this kind (a reader id) instead of recognising it.

output_directory.description: A folder that doesn't exist yet; its parent must.

path.description: Absolute path of the file; the active target when omitted.

paths.description: Exact member paths to take out.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_person_ask
tools.description: Ask the person a question in the app and wait for the answer: a short question, up to six suggested answers shown as buttons, and optionally a typed reply. Use it when a choice changes the result (scope, style, which feature first) and you can't decide from the evidence. Returns the answer text, or a note to continue with your best judgement if nobody answers within 30 minutes.

allow_text.description: Accept a typed answer too (default true).

choices.description: Up to six short suggested answers, best first.

context.description: One or two sentences of context shown under the question.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_plan_update
tools.description: Replace the plan with a numbered list of steps, each todo/doing/done/blocked with a short why. Pass based_on_revision to avoid overwriting someone else's update.

based_on_revision.description: The revision your change is based on (from core_investigation_show); omit to overwrite.

steps.description: The whole plan, in order (replaces the previous one).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_report_save
tools.description: Save a report a client composed (Markdown, HTML or plain text) to an absolute path the person chose. Only .md, .html, .htm or .txt files.

path.description: Where to save it: an absolute path ending in .md, .html, .htm or .txt.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_report_write
tools.description: Turn the investigation (brief, plan, findings, hypotheses, handoff) and the evidence ledger into a readable report: what we looked at, what we found (each finding with its plain-English summary, confidence and cited evidence), open questions, and how it was done. format=markdown (default) or html. With an absolute path it writes the file (WRITES_FILESYSTEM); otherwise it returns the text.

format.description: markdown (default) or html. HTML is a self-contained styled page.

include_evidence.description: Include the full evidence ledger as an appendix (default true). Findings always cite ids.

path.description: Absolute path to write the report to. When omitted the text is returned instead.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_session_show
tools.description: What's open, which target is active, Clean room or Deep mode, evidence and unknown counts, version.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_target_close
tools.description: Close the active target (or the one named). Evidence stays in the project.

target_id.description: Target to close; the active one when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_target_open
tools.description: Open a file, app bundle or folder as the active target. Detects what it is from its contents. For raw machine code pass format=raw-binary with architecture and entry_point.

architecture.description: Required with raw-binary: x86, x86_64, arm, arm64.

language_id.description:
Optional Deep-mode processor pin: a Ghidra language id such as `RISCV:LE:64:RV64GC`,
`PowerPC:BE:32:default`, `6502:LE:16:default`, `MIPS:BE:32:default` or `ARM:LE:32:v7`.
Takes effect only in Deep mode (Ghidra); it lets Deep target processors the built-in
clean-room engine doesn't cover, and overrides the `ghidra.language_id` setting for this
target. Ignored in Clean room.

path.description: Absolute path to a file, app bundle or folder.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_target_select
tools.description: Make another open target the active one.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_target_triage
tools.description: Say what a file is in plain English (format, OS, architecture, language/toolchain hints such as Go, Rust, .NET, Electron, Flutter, Delphi, packers) and which toolsets and tools to use next. Uses the active target unless path is given.

path.description: Absolute path of a file or folder; the active target when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_targets_list
tools.description: Every open target with its id, kind and sha256.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_unknown_add
tools.description: Record something not yet known, with what would settle it.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_unknown_edit
tools.description: Change an unknown's status, evidence or resolution. Pass based_on_revision; a stale revision gives stale_revision.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_unknown_verify
tools.description: Check that a resolved unknown has a resolution and cites evidence that exists and is intact.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__core_unknowns_show
tools.description: Recorded unknowns, filtered by status, severity or domain.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__db_sqlite_show
tools.description: Read a SQLite 3 database file without running any SQL: the header (page size, page count, text encoding, SQLite version that wrote it, WAL mode, freelist), the schema from sqlite_schema (tables, indexes, views and triggers with their CREATE statements and, for tables, parsed column names and types), per-table row counts (counted by walking the b-tree, bounded), and a page of rows from a named table (offset/limit; values as JSON; BLOBs shown as length plus a SHA-256 prefix, never dumped). Everything is bounded and read-only. Built-in parser (no SQLite library).

path.description: Absolute path of a .sqlite/.db file; the active target when omitted.

table.description: Read a page of rows from this table (by name, case-insensitive). Omit to list the schema only.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__engines_adb_check
tools.description: Report whether Android platform-tools (adb) is installed (Settings path, the managed engine store, then PATH) and its version. Contacts no device. Needs nothing installed to answer.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__engines_apktool_check
tools.description: Report whether Apktool is installed (Settings path, managed engine store, then PATH) and its version. Craft Anything's built-in resource and manifest decoders need nothing installed; Apktool is optional.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__engines_app_open
tools.description: Open Unity Hub or the Epic Games Launcher (to sign in and install the Unity Editor or Unreal Engine), found on this computer. Only those two; nothing else is started.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__engines_install
tools.description: Download and install an engine into Craft Anything's own folder: `ghidra` (Deep mode, with its Java), `godot`, or any engine with a pinned download (`adb`, `jadx`...). Every download is checked against its published SHA-256. Unity and Unreal need their vendors' installers and accounts: on Windows the installer (Unity Hub, the Epic Games Launcher) is downloaded, its publisher checked, and opened for the person; elsewhere they get the download page.

engine.description: `ghidra`, `godot`, `unity`, `unreal`, or an engine id from engines_list.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__engines_jeb_check
tools.description: Connect to the user-run JEB MCP server set in Settings → Engines (jeb_url, loopback only), report its server information, upstream tools and client information. Never starts JEB.

timeout_secs.description: Seconds to wait for the whole exchange (1..=600).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__engines_list
tools.description: What's on this computer: each external engine (where it was found, what it's for, whether it can be installed for you), Ghidra for Deep mode, and the game engines that can build games (Unity, Unreal, Godot, Rust) with whether each is ready.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__engines_tshark_check
tools.description: Check whether Wireshark's tshark is installed (Settings → Engines, the engine store, PATH, or the standard Wireshark folder) and which version it reports. Reads no capture. Optional: the built-in capture decoder works without it.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__firmware_image_extract
tools.description: Carve every recognised region of a firmware image into a new folder (output_directory must not exist yet), decompress gzip/zlib/xz/LZMA/bzip2/Zstandard streams, unpack ZIP, tar and cpio members and boot-image payloads, list and extract files from squashfs, cramfs, romfs, ext2/3/4 and (best-effort) JFFS2 filesystems, and repeat on what comes out up to max_depth levels. Bounded by max_output_bytes and max_output_files; never overwrites; members or filesystem paths that would escape the folder and links are refused. Writes manifest.json listing every output with its SHA-256 and how it was unpacked.

limit.description: Outputs listed in the evidence (the manifest always lists all of them; 1..=5000, default 500).

max_output_bytes.description: Most bytes written in total (up to 512 MiB, default 256 MiB).

output_directory.description: Absolute path of a folder that does not exist yet; it is created (its parent must exist).

path.description: Absolute path of the image; the active target when omitted.

range.description: Only extract from this part of the file.

length.description: Bytes in the range (cut to the end of the file).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__firmware_regions_list
tools.description: Signature scan of a firmware image or disk dump with the built-in engine: compression streams (gzip, zlib, xz, LZMA, bzip2, Zstandard, LZ4), archives (ZIP, tar, cpio, 7z, RAR, CAB), filesystems (squashfs, cramfs, romfs, JFFS2, UBI/UBIFS, ext2/3/4, FAT, ISO 9660), boot images (legacy boot-loader images, Android boot), device trees/FIT, executables (ELF, PE, Mach-O) and PEM blocks, each checked against its header; plus an entropy map, coverage, gaps and unexplained high-entropy spans. Regions are paged (offset/limit); range limits the scan to part of the file.

entropy_block.description: Entropy block size in bytes (256..=1048576, default 4096). Grows when the map would exceed 4096 blocks.

path.description: Absolute path of the image; the active target when omitted.

range.description: Only scan this part of the file (offsets stay relative to the whole file).

length.description: Bytes in the range (cut to the end of the file).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__formats_ai_weights_show
tools.description: Read an AI model file's header: GGUF (versions 2 and 3) or safetensors. Architecture, name, quantization, approximate parameter count, metadata keys and values (long values shortened), and tensors with their types and shapes, paged (offset/limit). Reads at most max_header_bytes from the start of the file, so very large models are fine; tensor data is never read. Uses the active target unless path is given.

max_header_bytes.description: Most bytes read from the start of the file (1 KiB..4 GiB, default 256 MiB).

path.description: Absolute path of the model file; the active target when omitted.

Detail.description:
The uniform summary-first detail control (see the module docs). `complete` is the default and
returns the full evidence record; `summary` returns a compact, pageable view.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__formats_bytecode_show
tools.description: Read a CPython compiled file (.pyc): the Python version from its magic number, how it ties to its source (modification time and size, or a source hash), and, for Python 3.8 to 3.14, its compiled code: each module, class and function with its name, dotted name, source file, first line, argument counts, the names it uses and the text among its constants, paged with offset/limit, parents before children. Other versions report the header and say why. python_version reads a file of bare marshalled code, such as a script taken out of a PyInstaller program. Built-in; nothing is executed and bytecode isn't decoded.

path.description: Absolute path of the file; the active target when omitted.

python_version.description: Treat the file as bare marshalled code with no header, compiled by this Python ("3.12").

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__formats_evm_interface_show
tools.description: Find the public function selectors in EVM contract bytecode (raw or hex, from a file or inline): where the dispatcher sends each selector, whether the function refuses payments (CALLVALUE check), fallback/receive presence, binary-search dispatch, and the compiler metadata (solc/vyper version, IPFS/Swarm hash). Function names are not recoverable without an ABI. Never executes the code.

bytecode.description: The bytecode as a hex string (optional 0x), instead of a file.

path.description: Absolute path of a file holding the bytecode; the active target when neither path nor bytecode is given.

oneOf.description: Hex when the content is only hex digits (optional 0x), raw bytes otherwise.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__formats_sbpf_disassemble
tools.description: Disassemble a range of eBPF / Solana sBPF bytecode into an instruction listing (address, mnemonic, operands, and resolved jump/call targets). Give a file (ELF with EM_BPF, or raw bytecode with encoding=raw) and an optional byte offset and length into the code. Built-in decoder; nothing is executed.

assume_version.description: Override the sBPF version (and the version for raw bytecode).

length.description: Bytes to disassemble from `offset` (default: to the end, capped).

offset.description: Byte offset into the code (the .text section for ELF, the file for raw). Default 0.

path.description: Absolute path of the program file; the active target when omitted.

oneOf.description: ELF when the file starts with the ELF magic, raw bytecode otherwise.
Force ELF parsing (machine type EM_BPF).
Treat the whole file as raw sBPF bytecode (no ELF, no sections or syscalls).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__formats_sbpf_show
tools.description: Inspect a Solana on-chain program or classic eBPF object (an ELF whose machine type is EM_BPF=247): the sBPF version (guessed from e_flags), sections (.text, .rodata, relocation tables), the dynamic symbol table, relocations with their R_BPF_* types, the syscalls it calls (resolved by the murmur3 hash of the helper name — sol_log_, sol_invoke_signed_*, ...), the entrypoint, discovered functions with basic blocks, and a paged disassembly listing with jump/call targets and a small pseudo form. Built-in decoder; nothing is executed. Honest limits: no account-model semantics and no Anchor IDL unless supplied separately.

assume_version.description: Override the sBPF version instead of the e_flags guess (and the version for raw bytecode).

offset.description: First instruction of the disassembly page.

path.description: Absolute path of the program file; the active target when omitted.

oneOf.description: Format, version, section/syscall/function counts and the entrypoint.
Everything, with the disassembly listing paged.
ELF when the file starts with the ELF magic, raw bytecode otherwise.
Force ELF parsing (machine type EM_BPF).
Treat the whole file as raw sBPF bytecode (no ELF, no sections or syscalls).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__formats_wasm_compare
tools.description: Compare the imports and exports of two WebAssembly modules (absolute paths): each import by module and name, each export by name, with its kind (func, table, memory, global, tag) and exact signature (function parameter/result types, memory and table limits, global type). Lists what was added, removed or changed, paged, with counts including unchanged entries; scope picks imports, exports or both. Static comparison only: matching signatures do not prove the modules behave the same.

left_path.description: Absolute path of the older (left) .wasm module.

right_path.description: Absolute path of the newer (right) .wasm module.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__formats_wasm_module_show
tools.description: Validate a WebAssembly module and list its sections, imports, exports, functions (signature, body size, name), memories, tables, globals, custom sections (names, producers, target features, source map URL), start function and data segments; optionally the text form (WAT), paged by characters; optionally scan JavaScript glue files for .wasm references and matching import names. Built-in parser.

include_wat.description: Include a page of the text form (WAT). Only valid modules are rendered.

js_glue_files.description: Up to 16 absolute paths of JavaScript glue files to scan for .wasm references and import names.

path.description: Absolute path of a .wasm file; the active target when omitted.

wat_offset.description: First character of the WAT page.

oneOf.description: Counts, validation, exports and producers.
Everything, with functions paged.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__frida_devices_find
tools.description: List devices Frida can see with `frida-ls-devices` (local, usb, remote). Pass remote to get one entry for a remote address without contacting it, so its reachability and auth are unverified (`frida-ps -H` checks it); its auth is forwarded to the CLI and never returned.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__frida_instrument_run
tools.description: Attach to (or spawn) a target, run a script for duration_ms (0..60000, default 1000), capture its output, and detach — all in one call. Executes foreign code, so it is consent-gated and destructive.

duration_ms.description: How long to run the script, in milliseconds (0..60000).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__frida_script_forget
tools.description: Forget a loaded script in a session (record-keeping; the bounded CLI run that executed it has already ended).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__frida_script_run
tools.description: Load and run an instrumentation script in a session for a bounded window, capturing its console/send output. source_kind=inline with source, or source_kind=file with an absolute path. Executing a script runs foreign code, so this is consent-gated and changes the target.

path.description: Absolute path to a script file (source_kind=file).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__frida_session_begin
tools.description: Begin a managed Frida session. mode=attach needs pid; mode=spawn needs program (absolute) and optional argv. Returns a session_id (held in memory) you pass to the other Frida tools. This records the session; code runs only when you load or resume a script.

argv.description: Extra arguments for a spawned program.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__frida_session_continue
tools.description: Resume a spawned, paused session so the target runs. Executes foreign code (the target's own), so this is consent-gated.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__frida_session_end
tools.description: End a managed session and forget it. Never kills the target process.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__frida_session_show
tools.description: Report a managed session's state, its device/target, and the scripts run in it with their most recent captured messages.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__frida_targets_list
tools.description: List processes and installed apps on the selected device with `frida-ps`. Give exactly one of device_id or remote.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__game_archives_list
tools.description: Find the packed files in a game's folder (absolute path): Unreal paks (.pak, checked by their footer) and IoStore containers (.utoc), Unity serialized files (.assets, level<n>, globalgamemanagers) and bundles (.bundle, data.unity3d), and Godot packs (.pck, or carried at the end of a program, checked by their mark, with how many files each declares), each with its size and the tool that lists it. Looks at most 8 folders deep and at 20000 entries.

path.description: Absolute path of the game's folder.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__game_iostore_list
tools.description: List what's inside an Unreal Engine IoStore container (absolute path of its .utoc table of contents, or of the .ucas beside it): its version, flags (compressed, encrypted, signed, indexed), compression methods, chunk and partition counts, and every named file with its size, stored size and compression, paged and optionally filtered by a part of the path. Unreal 5 games keep most of their assets this way. An encrypted container's names need the game's AES key, so they're counted, never guessed.

filter.description: Only files whose path contains this (any case).

path.description:
Absolute path of the archive (.pak, an IoStore container's .utoc or .ucas, a Unity .assets
or level file, or a Unity bundle).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__game_pak_extract
tools.description: Copy files out of an Unreal Engine .pak archive (absolute path). `file` is one file's path as game_pak_list shows it (any case) and `output` an absolute path that doesn't exist yet (its folders are made); the result has the size and SHA-256. A `file` ending in `/` (e.g. `Game/Content/UI/`) takes out every file under that folder into the folder `output`, keeping their layout, up to `limit` files per call: files already there are skipped, so calling again carries on. Stored and zlib-compressed files are supported and streamed. Encrypted files need the game's AES key and Oodle-compressed ones need Oodle (a commercial library the game ships), so both are refused with the reason.

file.description:
The file to take out, as game_pak_list shows it (e.g. `Game/Content/Maps/Level.umap`; any case),
or a folder ending in `/` (e.g. `Game/Content/UI/`) to take out every file under it.

limit.description: For a folder: the most files to take out in this call (at most 5000).

output.description:
Where to write it: an absolute path that doesn't exist yet (its folders are made). For a
folder, the folder to write into; files keep their layout under it.

path.description: Absolute path of the .pak file.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__game_pak_list
tools.description: List what's inside an Unreal Engine .pak archive (absolute path): its version (1-11), mount point, compression methods, and every file with its size, stored size, compression and whether it's encrypted, paged and optionally filtered by a part of the path. Only the footer and index are read, so very large paks are fine. An encrypted index is reported, never guessed: listing it needs the game's own AES key. Says when the game also keeps IoStore containers (.utoc/.ucas) beside it.

filter.description: Only files whose path contains this (any case).

path.description:
Absolute path of the archive (.pak, an IoStore container's .utoc or .ucas, a Unity .assets
or level file, or a Unity bundle).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__game_unity_asset_export
tools.description: Save one object of a Unity serialized file (absolute path of a .assets or level file, or of a bundle: then `file` picks the serialized file inside, the first by default) as a file anyone can open: a texture (Texture2D, by its path_id from game_unity_list) becomes a PNG at `output` (an absolute path that doesn't exist yet). Pixels are read inside the object or from the .resS file it streams from. Formats: Alpha8, R8, RGB24, RGBA32, ARGB32, BGRA32, RGB565, RGBA4444, ARGB4444, RHalf, RGHalf, RGBAHalf, RFloat, RGFloat, RGBAFloat, DXT1, DXT5, BC4, BC5, BC6H and BC7. Floating-point colours are shown in 8-bit sRGB and clip at white. Other formats (crunched, ASTC, ETC...) are refused with their name. Unity 2017.3 and later.

file.description: For a bundle: the serialized file inside it (as game_unity_bundle_list shows); the first by default.

output.description: Where to write it: an absolute path that doesn't exist yet (its folders are made).

path.description: Absolute path of the .assets or level file, or of a bundle.

path_id.description: The object's path id (game_unity_list shows them).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__game_unity_bundle_list
tools.description: List the files inside a Unity asset bundle in the UnityFS format (absolute path: a .bundle, data.unity3d or Addressables file): its format, Unity version, block compression (LZMA, LZ4), and each file with its size, and for each serialized file inside, its Unity version, object count and objects by class. Only the blocks that hold those files' headers are decompressed. Paged and optionally filtered by a part of the path.

filter.description: Only files whose path contains this (any case).

path.description:
Absolute path of the archive (.pak, an IoStore container's .utoc or .ucas, a Unity .assets
or level file, or a Unity bundle).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__game_unity_code_names_show
tools.description: Read a Unity IL2CPP global-metadata.dat (path: the file, or a game's folder, where it's found under *_Data/il2cpp_data/Metadata or Data/il2cpp_data/Metadata): the metadata version, its assemblies (images) and how many types, methods, fields and string literals it names. view picks a list to page: images, types (namespace, name, assembly, method and field counts), methods (name, declaring type, parameter count) or strings (the string literals, each shown up to 4096 bytes); contains keeps rows holding that text (any case). Versions 24 (its later 264-byte-header form), 27, 29 and 31 are read, each only after the file proves it fits; other versions give their header and say so. Many games change or encrypt this file: that's stated plainly and nothing is decrypted or guessed. Only names are here, with no code or addresses.

contains.description: Keep only rows holding this text (any case).

offset.description: First matching row of the page.

path.description: Absolute path of global-metadata.dat, or of a game's folder to find it in.

view.description: What to list: summary (the default), images, types, methods or strings.

oneOf.description: Counts and the first page of images.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__game_unity_list
tools.description: List the objects in a Unity serialized file (absolute path: a .assets file, level<n>, globalgamemanagers, sharedassets<n>.assets in <Game>_Data) or in a bundle (.bundle, data.unity3d: every serialized file inside it, each object naming its `file`, or only `file`'s): the format version, Unity version, build platform, how many objects of each class (GameObject, Texture2D, AudioClip, MonoBehaviour...), the other files it points to, and the objects with their path id, class, size and name (named assets, GameObjects and MonoBehaviours), paged and optionally filtered by class or name. Unity 5 and later.

file.description: For a bundle: only this serialized file inside it (as game_unity_bundle_list shows); every one by default.

filter.description: Only objects whose class or name contains this (any case).

path.description: Absolute path of the .assets or level file, or of a bundle.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__game_unreal_texture_export
tools.description: Save a texture of an Unreal Engine 4.26-4.27 game as a PNG, only when the person confirms they may unpack the game (permission: true; they made it or its rights holder allows it). path is the game's .pak (then `file` is the texture's .uasset path inside it, as game_pak_list shows it) or a .uasset already taken out, with its .uexp (and .ubulk) beside it. The largest mip the game ships is saved at `output` (an absolute path that doesn't exist yet). Formats: B8G8R8A8, R8G8B8A8, G8, A8, DXT1, DXT5, BC4, BC5, BC6H (tone-mapped to 8 bits) and BC7; others (ASTC...) are refused by name, as are Oodle-compressed and encrypted paks, Unreal 5 packages and packages written without property names.

file.description: For a pak: the texture's .uasset path inside it, as game_pak_list shows it.

output.description: Where to write the PNG: an absolute path that doesn't exist yet (its folders are made).

path.description: Absolute path of the game's .pak, or of a .uasset already taken out (its .uexp and .ubulk beside it).

permission.description: The person made this game or has its rights holder's permission to unpack its files.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__harmony_app_graph_build
tools.description: Project a HarmonyOS package's inventory (core_archive_show evidence or a path) into an application graph: module manifests, HAP/HSP packages, Ark bytecode, native libraries by ABI and resources.

inventory.description: core_archive_show evidence (inline or retained). Its recorded path is re-read for the full inventory.

path.description: Or an absolute path to inventory now. Defaults to the active target when neither is given.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__java_archive_show
tools.description: Read a JAR or WAR with the built-in parser: the MANIFEST.MF attributes (main class, class-path, versions), the classes it defines grouped into a package tree, bundled dependencies (nested jars and native libraries), resources, and the class-file (Java) version(s) seen.

path.description: Absolute path of the JAR/WAR; the active target when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__java_class_show
tools.description: One class from a JAR/WAR or a bare .class: its Java version, access flags, superclass, interfaces, source file, annotations, inner classes, and its fields and methods with Java-style signatures. With decompile=true, also a pseudo-Java skeleton of the class.

decompile.description: Also include a pseudo-Java skeleton of the class (confidence Inferred).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__java_class_users_find
tools.description: Every instruction in every class of a JAR/WAR (or a single .class) that calls, reads, writes, creates or casts to a class (or only calls one of its methods when method_name is given), with the calling method and bytecode offset. Paged.

method_name.description: Only calls to methods with this name.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__java_classes_find
tools.description: Search the classes (and optionally methods) defined in a JAR/WAR or a single .class by name; an empty query lists every class. Paged (offset/limit).

query.description: Case-insensitive part of a class (or method) name. Empty lists every class.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__java_method_show
tools.description: A method's JVM bytecode as a disassembly listing with resolved constant-pool references (fields, methods, classes, string/number constants), branch targets, switch tables and the exception table, plus a best-effort structured pseudo-Java reconstruction (confidence Inferred). Paged over instructions.

descriptor.description: The method descriptor (`(I)I`) to pick a specific overload; the first match otherwise.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__java_vineflower_decompile
tools.description: Decompile a Java .class file or JAR (absolute path or the active target) to Java source with Vineflower, run as a program (its .jar with the configured Java, or a vineflower script; set its path in Settings → Engines). Without class: the decompiled source files with their line counts, paged with offset/limit (and the source itself when there is one file). With class (com.example.Foo or com/example/Foo): that class's source, paged by lines; inner classes are inside their outer class's file. Optional engine.

class.description: One class to show (com.example.Foo or com/example/Foo).

limit.description: Files or lines per page (1–20000, default 2000).

offset.description: First file (or, with class, first line) of the page.

path.description: Absolute path of a .class or .jar; omit to use the active target.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__js_app_map
tools.description: Static analysis of an Electron app (app.asar or unpacked folder), a web bundle folder, a ZIP or a single script into an application graph: package and entry points (main, preload, renderer), BrowserWindow webPreferences, the IPC channel map (ipcMain.handle/on ↔ ipcRenderer.invoke/send, contextBridge members), module imports, bundler and chunk splitting (webpack, esbuild, browserify; Vite/Rollup detected), routes, HTTP endpoints, storage, platform effects, native modules, vendors and source maps. Built-in parser; nothing is executed.

include_node_modules.description: Also parse code under node_modules (off: only their package.json files are read, as vendor facts).

input_path.description: Absolute path of an app.asar, an unpacked Electron app or web bundle folder, a ZIP, or one .js/.html file.

limit.description: Modules per page in the result (the graph itself is always complete up to max_nodes).

offset.description: First module of the module page in the result.

source_paths.description: Extra absolute files or folders to include (for example an `app.asar.unpacked` folder kept elsewhere).

oneOf.description: Detect from the path: folder, ASAR, ZIP or single file.
Stop when an ASAR integrity hash does not match its file.
Record the mismatch as a limitation and continue.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__js_electron_fuses_show
tools.description: Read the Electron fuse wire from a packaged Electron app without running it: pass the main executable (Windows .exe, Linux binary), the macOS .app bundle or Electron Framework binary, or the app's folder. Reports each wire's file offset, version and declared length, and every fuse by index with its name (RunAsNode, EnableCookieEncryption, EnableNodeOptionsEnvironmentVariable, EnableNodeCliInspectArguments, EnableEmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation, OnlyLoadAppFromAsar, LoadBrowserProcessSpecificV8Snapshot, GrantFileProtocolExtraPrivileges, WasmTrapHandlers), state (enabled, disabled, removed), raw byte, what that state means for security, and whether it is the hardened setting. No sentinel means the fuse state is unknown.

path.description: Absolute path of the Electron executable, macOS .app bundle, Electron Framework binary or app folder; the active target when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__js_electron_page_show
tools.description: Passively inspect one Electron renderer page (a hostless file:// page) over CDP: frame origins, a DOM summary, parsed scripts (optionally their sources) and, opt-in, console entries. Never navigates or evaluates; values are never kept.

target_id.description: The renderer target id (from js_electron_pages_list); the first renderer otherwise.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__js_electron_pages_list
tools.description: List the debuggable targets of an Electron app started with --remote-debugging-port (loopback), labelling renderer pages (file:// or app:// URLs) and other targets. Attach-only discovery over HTTP.

cdp_endpoint.description: Loopback CDP endpoint of the Electron app (it must be started with --remote-debugging-port).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__js_electron_walkthrough_record
tools.description: Launch an Electron app's own executable with a private profile and a loopback debugging port, run a short script (wait / reload / navigate / click) against its first renderer, capture network request outlines, then terminate the owned process. Executes the app and accesses the network, so it needs your approval.

application_executable.description: Absolute path of the Electron app's executable to launch.

args.description: Extra arguments passed to the app after the debugging flags.

startup_secs.description: Seconds to wait for the app to start its debugging port.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__js_exports_compare
tools.description: Compare what each module exports (ES module names, CommonJS names, the kind of module.exports) between two application graphs, matching modules by path then by structure.

left.description: The older version: js_app_map evidence or an absolute path.

right.description: The newer version, in the same forms.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__js_function_explain
tools.description: Function-level slice of an application graph: for the seeded functions, their calls (resolved where possible), callers (resolved or same-name inferred), strings, the IPC/effects/endpoints/storage they touch, and a depth-limited callee tree. Unresolved dynamic calls are listed.

application.description: js_app_map evidence or an absolute path to analyse.

oneOf.description: Case-insensitive substring.

value.description: What to look for: a channel name, function name, string, module path, URL fragment or node id.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__js_runtime_code_match
tools.description: Match app graph evidence against what was seen running (captured scripts with URLs and sha256): each static module is loaded, resident in a loaded bundle, loaded with different content, not observed, or unknown; runtime-only scripts are listed. Pure computation over evidence.

runtime_evidence.description: Runtime evidence that lists scripts (objects with `url` and `sha256`), inline or retained.

static_evidence.description: The static side: one or more application graphs.

evidence.description: js_app_map evidence (inline or {"kind":"saved","evidence_id":...}) or an absolute path.

role.description: `application`, `cache` or `assets`.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__js_runtime_watch
tools.description: Attach the V8 inspector to one Node/Electron target and observe passively: it sends exactly Runtime.enable and Debugger.enable, then records the scripts parsed (deduplicated and sorted), execution contexts and a parse-failure count. Never resumes a paused (--inspect-brk) target. runtime_kind is taken as given.

runtime_kind.description: The kind of runtime, as given (not checked).

target_id.description: The target id to observe (from js_runtimes_list); the first otherwise.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__js_runtimes_list
tools.description: List the inspectable targets of a Node or Electron process started with --inspect (loopback V8 inspector endpoint), with their ids and whether another client is attached. Attach-only discovery.

cdp_endpoint.description: Loopback V8 inspector endpoint, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:9229 (node --inspect=127.0.0.1:9229).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__js_source_bundle_compare
tools.description: Match reference source files (from app_source_import, or a folder path) to the shipped app's files and bundle modules by path, source-map listing, shared strings, function names and export names; reports matches with scores and reasons, unmatched sources and bundle code without a source.

application.description: js_app_map evidence or an absolute path to analyse.

source.description: app_source_import evidence (inline or retained) or an absolute source folder path.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__js_source_locate
tools.description: Map a position in generated (bundled/minified) JavaScript back to its original file, line, column and name through a source map (a .map file, a script's sourceMappingURL, or an inline data: map). Lines are 1-based, columns 0-based UTF-16. Returns every original position at that point and nearby original source when the map embeds it.

context_lines.description: Original-source lines of context around each hit.

script_path.description: Or the generated script: its sourceMappingURL (a sibling file or an inline data: URL) is followed.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__js_sources_restore
tools.description: Turn minified bundles back into readable files in a new folder: split webpack/esbuild/browserify module tables into one file per module, pretty-print everything, apply safe unminify rewrites (!0→true, void 0→undefined, statement sequences, webpack module parameter names via scope analysis) and write original files embedded in source maps. manifest.json records every input digest, module byte range and output file.

additional_paths.description: Up to 16 more scripts or folders.

limit.description: Output files listed per page in the result.

output_directory.description: Absolute path of a folder that does not exist yet.

path.description: Absolute path of a script or a folder of scripts.

oneOf.description: Split only recognised bundle module tables; pretty-print everything; write source-map originals.
Pretty-print only (no splitting, no source-map originals).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__managed_app_graph_build
tools.description: Project a .NET assembly (managed evidence or a path) into an application graph: assembly, referenced assemblies, types, methods, external members, native modules and resources, joined by contains, references, inherits, calls and pinvoke edges. Bounded by max_nodes.

input.description: Managed evidence (managed_assembly_show, managed_members_list or managed_native_calls_list) or an absolute path; the active target when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__managed_assemblies_compare
tools.description: Compare the members of two assemblies (managed_members_list evidence or absolute paths) with tiered unique matching: identical IL and signature (survives renames), then type+name+signature, then the same structure. Reports unchanged, changed (body differs), renamed or moved, added, removed and ambiguous methods, plus added/removed types and fields.

left.description: The older build: managed_members_list evidence (inline, {"kind":"saved","evidence_id":...} or an id) or an absolute path.

right.description: The newer build, in the same forms.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__managed_assembly_show
tools.description: Built-in ECMA-335 reader: PE/CLI header (runtime version, IL-only/32-bit/strong-name flags, entry point, ReadyToRun), metadata streams and table row counts, assembly identity, assembly and module references, manifest resources, forwarded types, assembly attributes (TargetFramework decoded) and a classification (runtime family, implementation, managed architecture). Uses the active target unless path is given.

path.description: Absolute path of a .NET assembly (.dll/.exe); the active target when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__managed_ilspy_decompile
tools.description: Decompile a .NET assembly (absolute path or the active target) with the installed ILSpy command line (ilspycmd): operation decompile gives C# for the whole assembly, or for one type with type_name (`Namespace.Type`, nested types as `Outer+Inner`); il gives the whole assembly's IL; list_types lists its classes, interfaces, structs, delegates and enums. Its update check is turned off, so it never goes online. Returns the raw text paged by lines. Optional engine: the built-in .NET tools need nothing installed.

offset.description: First output line of the page.

path.description: Absolute path of the assembly; the active target when omitted.

type_name.description: For decompile: one fully qualified type (`Namespace.Type`, nested as `Outer+Inner`).

oneOf.description: C# source.
The IL, for the whole assembly.
Every class, interface, struct, delegate and enum, one per line.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__managed_members_list
